physics_goals.quote: The CERN Axion Solar Telescope (CAST) is an experiment to search for hypothetical particles called 'axions'.
physics_goals.value: Search for axions produced in the Sun's core by pointing a strong dipole magnet at the Sun and looking for X-rays from axion-to-photon conversion

summary.plain: CAST looked for axions, hypothetical particles that might explain dark matter, by pointing a powerful magnet left over from Large Hadron Collider testing at the Sun and watching for X-rays. It ran at CERN from 2003 until the end of 2022.
summary.technical: Axion helioscope at CERN using a decommissioned LHC test dipole magnet (reusing former LEP DELPHI cryogenics) tracking the Sun, with X-ray optics and detectors at the bores; proposed 1999, approved 2000, data taking 2003-06-18 to 2022-12-31 (completed) per its INSPIRE/Greybook record.

unique_capabilities.quote: a prototype of a dipole magnet for the Large Hadron Collider, with its hollow beam pipes acting as viewing tubes
unique_capabilities.value: Reuses a decommissioned LHC prototype superconducting dipole magnet, with its beam-pipe bores as viewing tubes, tracking the Sun on a moving platform
